profile.summary: OmniReg-GPT is a generative DNA foundation model for long human genomic sequences. It reads DNA tokenised into subword units and was pretrained to predict the next token on 20 kb windows of the human T2T genome. Its embeddings are fine-tuned for regulatory tasks such as histone marks, promoters and enhancers, gene expression, chromatin accessibility and 3D chromatin contacts, and it can generate candidate enhancer sequences from a prompt.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper: Abstract; Methods, Training procedure; README: introduction

summary_quotes.text: a generative foundation model designed for the low-resource pretraining of long genomic sequences by optimized attention mechanism
we pretrained OmniReg-GPT on the human reference genome using 20 kb sequence windows

including predicting histone modifications, CpG methylation, transcription factor binding sites, context dependent gene expression, single-cell chromatin accessibility, 3D chromatin contact and generating cell-type-specific enhancers
OmniReg-GPT also holds the potential to generate candidate cell-type-specific enhancers through prompt engineering

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: OmniReg-GPT is a decoder-only transformer trained with next-token prediction. DNA is tokenised with the BPE tokenizer from GENA-LM (vocabulary 32,000). The network has 12 local blocks, where each window of tokens attends to itself and the preceding window, and 2 global blocks that build a whole-sequence representation. The authors say this reduces attention cost from quadratic to linear in sequence length. It uses rotary position embeddings and FlashAttention. For downstream tasks a single vector is taken as the mean of all token embeddings.

We then processed these sentences using Gena’s tokenizer, which is configured with a dictionary size of 32,000.
OmniReg-GPT consists 12 local blocks for generating contextual embeddings and 2 global blocks for constructing comprehensive sequence representations
Then a local window attention is employed, allowing attention to be performed with both the preceding window and the sequence itself.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: One set of pretrained weights is released on Zenodo (record 14893616, 2025-02-19) as a single pytorch_model.bin of 1,143,401,937 bytes. The paper reports a 270 million parameter model and also mentions a 138 million parameter variant with hidden dimension 768 in its memory comparison; the Zenodo record does not say which variant the file is. The code is also archived on Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.16933275), and downstream datasets are in Zenodo record 14883459. A result should name the repository commit and the Zenodo weights record; this page read commit 7cae626d.

run_guide.summary: Set up the OmniReg-GPT environment at a pinned commit and download the tokenizer and pretrained weights needed by the fine-tuning and generation scripts.
prerequisites: conda, for a Python 3.8 environment; PyTorch 2.0 or later (the README pins torch==2.0.1).
GPU needs for inference are not stated.
